items.display_name: Available Water Capacity (0-100 cm root zone)

provenance.formula: AWC_layer = theta(33 kPa) - theta(1500 kPa); root-zone AWC = (5*0-5cm, 10*5-15cm, 15*15-30cm, 30*30-60cm, 40*60-100cm) / 100
provenance.aggregation_method: spatial reduction per SoilGrids layer, then thickness-weighted mean over the 0-100 cm root zone
limitations: This is a difference of two modelled predictions, so its uncertainty is larger than either input's.

The 33 kPa and 1500 kPa conventions inherit all the limitations of the field-capacity and wilting-point surrogates they are built from. In soils where either convention is a poor approximation, the available water figure inherits the error.
At 250 m within-field soil variability is not resolved, and a water balance built on this figure alone will mis-irrigate any field whose soil varies within the cell.
This is a soil-water storage context figure. It is not an irrigation prescription, a yield forecast or a drought diagnosis.

SoilGrids is a static modelled prediction produced once from a global compilation of soil profiles. It carries no observation date, is not a time series, and does not describe any change the soil has undergone since the profiles were sampled. The requested period is the analysis context, not an observation window.

Field capacity and wilting point are approximated by the water content at 33 kPa and 1500 kPa suction respectively. This is the standard soil-physics convention, not a measurement of either quantity: field capacity is a dynamic property that depends on drainage history and profile structure, and the 33 kPa suction is a poorer approximation in coarse, strongly structured or shrink-swell soils than in uniform temperate soils.

The value is a thickness-weighted mean over the 0 to 100 cm interval, weighting each SoilGrids layer by its own thickness in centimetres 0-5cm (5 cm), 5-15cm (10 cm), 15-30cm (15 cm), 30-60cm (30 cm), 60-100cm (40 cm). An unweighted mean would implicitly treat these unequal layers as equally thick and would be wrong by an amount that depends on the profile. The 100-200 cm layer is excluded because it lies below the crop root zone.

Available water capacity is expressed as a volume fraction (cm3/cm3).
